newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil oilworkers go on two-hour warning strike.
newsitem.headline: Brazil oilworkers go on two-hour warning strike.

text.p: Brazil's oilworkers staged a two-hour warning strike on Thursday after annual salary talks with state-owned oil company Petrobras broke down, a spokeswoman for the United Oilworkers' Federation (FUP) said.

Leila Costa said the stoppage between 7 a.m. and 9 a.m. local time did not affect production and refinery output. She said only after two days of work stoppage would there be any affect on production.

Pay negotiations between Petrobras and the FUP, which represents Brazil's 21 oilworker unions, broke down last week with Petrobras offering a 8.8 percent pay rise and the FUP asking for a 46.64 percent pay rise.
Costa said the FUP's consultative council which includes representatives from all the oilworkers unions would meet in two weeks to discuss the next move in the pay dispute.
She said the FUP was waiting for Petrobras to start new talks and negotiate its offer.
-- Simona de Logu, Rio de Janeiro newsroom, 5521 507 4151
